pre_cleanup_failure.faulting_operation: Memory::Initialize writes the title-specific constant 0x2A6E3F38 at guest 0x8000001C after mapping the guest arena.

before.same_offset_probe: A write to a shared mapping at file offset 0x80000000 raised SIGBUS.

orphaned_shm_cleanup.action: Removed only the 15 xenia_memory_* objects after checking /proc for active mappings and open file descriptors.

after.same_size_and_offset_probe: A 4.5 GiB shared-memory file accepted a write at offset 0x80000000.

post_cleanup_run.retail_progress: After cleanup, the same Linux executable initialized the retail runtime, opened the boot and persistent BFF archives, reached repeated guest draw and Copy/Convert work, and issued file requests from the frontend scene path.

interpretation.supported: The reproduced SIGBUS correlated with a large set of orphaned POSIX shared-memory objects. Removing objects with no live references restored the identical offset write and allowed the retail runtime to advance into boot archives and frontend asset requests.
interpretation.not_proven: The exact tmpfs quota or kernel resource mechanism behind SIGBUS was not isolated. This environment cleanup is not a code fix and does not establish that a fresh installation will encounter the same issue.
interpretation.frontend_limit: The repeated XML misses may be expected fallback probes or a fatal asset gap; the archive index has no exact XML member. No menu or offline race is proven by draw counts or file requests.
interpretation.ownership_limit: The repeated Vulkan frame-refresh warnings in the runtime log report a 4x versus 1x sample-count mismatch and remain in Process 2's renderer scope; no renderer files were changed.
